notes:
disagreement: case installed_product_id: one pass tests installed_product_id IS NULL, the other leaves it untested; kept IS NULL, the tighter predicate, because Globex holds no installed product of product 123 and the policy lets a case carry only an installed product of its own product and account.
disagreement: selector of the unpublished-article stay: one pass covers any article not in state published, the other article 188 alone; kept the wider selector, the tighter requirement, because the policy bars linking any unpublished article.
disagreement: notification type: one pass update, the other solution_proposal; chose solution_proposal because 'regarding latest updates' is everyday wording that names no type, the benchmark's check is the prior, and on the seed no update notification carries an article while the check attaches article 189.
disagreement: disposition of 'Case opened for HPE ProLiant DL380 Gen10 with Derek as the contact': one pass repaired, the other kept; chose repaired because the check's number = 'CS-0001233' is a server-kept column that is never a cell, so that predicate is dropped.
disagreement: disposition of 'Notification sent to Derek with the case and KB attached': one pass repaired it to type update, the other kept it; chose kept, following the notification type resolution.
Globex (account 4) holds no installed product of HPE ProLiant DL380 Gen10 (product 123) and no entitlement for that product; its active account-wide entitlements 28 and 30 (active contracts 9 and 10) cover the case, so the case carries the product and no installed product. The policy's check that the product belongs to the account is read as met through those entitlements; a stricter reading would bar the case, but the request asks for it outright. Entitlement verification is a read and leaves no row to test.
The notification type is the judgement most open to dispute: 'notify him regarding latest updates' could be read as type update, which on the seed never carries an article.
The case's short_description follows the policy template ('Product: ... Issue: is not working as expected.'), which the benchmark does not test, so it is left out. No assignment, escalation or SLA is asked for, and the case stays new.
